risk: Changes reach production without testing or approval, causing outages, data corruption or the quiet introduction of unauthorised functionality.
audit_objective: Confirm that changes to production systems are authorised, tested and traceable.
what_to_review: Change approval, testing evidence and back-out planning
Emergency change usage and retrospective approval
Segregation between development, testing and production migration
Direct data fixes applied to production databases
Post-implementation review of significant changes
procedures: Reconcile changes deployed to production against approved change records; investigate any deployment with no change ticket.
Quantify emergency changes as a proportion of total and test retrospective approval.
Test whether developers can migrate their own code to production.
Extract direct database changes and test authorisation for each.
Test back-out plans for substance rather than a generic statement.
red_flags: Emergency changes used to bypass approval routinely
Deployments with no corresponding ticket
Developers holding production migration rights
Testing evidence created after go-live
plain: Most major system outages are caused by a change someone made, not by an attacker.

risk: Batch failures, interface errors and processing exceptions go unnoticed, so financial data is incomplete or wrong without anyone knowing.
audit_objective: Confirm that scheduled processing and system interfaces run completely and that failures are detected and resolved.
what_to_review: Job scheduling, dependencies and failure alerting
Interface control totals between systems
Incident detection, prioritisation and resolution
Reprocessing and manual intervention controls
Monitoring coverage and who watches it out of hours
procedures: Review job failure logs for the period and test resolution of failures affecting financial data.
Test interface control totals between key systems and quantify unexplained differences.
Sample incidents and trace to root cause and permanent fix rather than a workaround.
Test who can amend the job schedule and whether changes follow change management.
red_flags: Recurring job failures accepted as normal
Interfaces reconciled by record count only, not value
Incidents closed as "restarted, no further action"
Schedule amendments made directly in production
plain: Overnight processing runs the business. When a job fails silently, the numbers are simply incomplete.

subprocess: Cyber Security — Vulnerability and Patch Management
risk: Known vulnerabilities remain unpatched on systems exposed to attack, giving an intruder a documented route in.
audit_objective: Assess whether vulnerabilities are identified, prioritised and remediated within defined timeframes.
what_to_review: Asset inventory completeness — you cannot patch what you do not know about
Vulnerability scanning coverage and frequency
Remediation timeframes by severity and adherence to them
Exception and risk acceptance process for unpatched systems
End-of-life and unsupported systems still in use
procedures: Compare the asset inventory to network discovery output and quantify unmanaged devices.
Extract open vulnerabilities by severity and age; quantify those beyond the remediation deadline.
Test the exception process for critical vulnerabilities accepted rather than fixed, and whether acceptance was authorised at the right level.
Identify end-of-life systems still in production and test the compensating controls claimed.
red_flags: Critical vulnerabilities open for months
Scanning that excludes the most sensitive network segments
Risk acceptances granted indefinitely
Unsupported operating systems on internet-facing hosts
evidence: Asset inventory and network discovery output
plain: Attackers use known weaknesses that already have fixes available. Unpatched systems are an open door.

subprocess: Cyber Security — Perimeter, Endpoint and Email
risk: An attacker gains entry through phishing, weak authentication or an unprotected endpoint, and moves through the network undetected.
audit_objective: Assess the preventive and detective controls against the most common intrusion routes.
what_to_review: Multi-factor authentication coverage, especially remote access and administrators
Email filtering, phishing simulation results and reporting culture
Endpoint protection deployment and exception devices
Network segmentation limiting lateral movement
Logging, monitoring and alert triage
procedures: Test multi-factor authentication coverage across all remote access paths and privileged accounts; identify bypass routes.
Review phishing simulation results by department and test whether repeat clickers receive intervention.
Reconcile endpoint protection deployment to the asset inventory and investigate unprotected devices.
Test segmentation by reviewing firewall rules between zones for overly permissive entries.
Sample security alerts and test triage quality and time to respond.
red_flags: Service and administrator accounts exempt from multi-factor authentication
Firewall rules permitting any-to-any
Alerts closed without investigation notes
Phishing reporting rates near zero
plain: Most breaches start with a person clicking something or a password being reused, not with sophisticated hacking.

risk: Backups exist but cannot actually restore the business, so a ransomware event or hardware failure becomes an existential problem.
audit_objective: Confirm that backup and recovery capability is real, tested and protected from the same event it insures against.
what_to_review: Backup scope, frequency and alignment to recovery point objectives
Restoration testing — actual restores, not backup success reports
Immutability and offline copies protected from ransomware
Disaster recovery plan currency and test realism
Recovery time objectives agreed with the business and validated
procedures: Obtain evidence of an actual restore test and its outcome; a successful backup job is not evidence of recoverability.
Test whether backup copies are immutable or offline and whether backup infrastructure uses separate credentials.
Compare recovery objectives agreed with the business to what the most recent test achieved.
Review the disaster recovery test scope — a tabletop exercise is not a failover.
red_flags: Backups never restored in test
Backup systems on the same domain with the same admin credentials
Recovery objectives defined by IT with no business input
DR tests scoped to exclude the critical systems
evidence: Backup job reports and restore test evidence
plain: Having backups is not the same as being able to restore. You find out which you have on the worst day.

risk: Critical systems run on third-party platforms with no assurance over their controls and no ability to exit.
audit_objective: Assess governance and assurance over outsourced and cloud-hosted technology.
what_to_review: Inventory of cloud services and shadow IT procured outside the process
Service auditor reports obtained and complementary user controls performed
Contractual terms — data location, breach notification, audit rights, exit
Cloud configuration and who is responsible for what
Vendor access to the organisation's environment
procedures: Build an independent inventory of cloud services from expenditure and network data; compare to the official register.
Obtain service auditor reports for critical providers, identify complementary user controls and test whether they operate.
Review cloud configuration against a recognised benchmark for the most sensitive workloads.
Test vendor remote access — accounts, authentication and session monitoring.
red_flags: Cloud services paid for on expense claims
Service auditor reports unread
Storage buckets or databases publicly accessible
Vendor accounts with standing privileged access
plain: Using a cloud provider moves the work, not the accountability. If it goes down, your business goes down.

risk: Personal and business-critical data is held without ownership, retained beyond need, or exposed to people who have no reason to see it.
audit_objective: Assess whether data is classified, owned, protected and retained in line with obligations.
what_to_review: Data inventory, classification and ownership
Retention schedules and their actual enforcement
Access to sensitive data sets and periodic review
Data quality controls at entry and in transformation
Privacy obligations — consent, subject rights, cross-border transfer
procedures: Test whether data classified as sensitive is actually protected accordingly, including in test environments and extracts.
Test retention by identifying data past its retention period and confirming whether deletion occurred.
Test data subject rights requests for completeness and timeliness of response.
Review data quality controls for key financial data feeds and quantify error rates.
Test whether production data is copied into non-production environments unmasked.
red_flags: Production data in test systems unmasked
Retention policy written but never executed
No named owner for critical data sets
Cross-border transfers with no assessed legal basis
plain: Data that nobody owns gets kept too long, shared too widely, and eventually leaked.

subprocess: IT Asset Management and Software Licensing
risk: Hardware and software are untracked, so assets are lost, licences are under-purchased and the organisation is exposed to audit by the vendor.
audit_objective: Confirm that technology assets and licences are tracked, reconciled and compliant.
what_to_review: Hardware asset register accuracy and disposal process
Data sanitisation on disposal or return of devices
Software discovery versus licences held
Licence terms — users, cores, virtualisation rights
Vendor audit history and settlements
procedures: Reconcile the asset register to network discovery and to procurement records; investigate differences in both directions.
Test disposal records for evidence of data sanitisation certificates.
Compare installed software counts to licence entitlements and quantify the compliance gap.
Review licence terms for the largest vendors against the deployment model actually used.
red_flags: Devices issued to leavers never returned
Disposal with no sanitisation evidence
Software deployed well beyond entitlement
Virtualisation increasing licence exposure unnoticed
plain: Untracked laptops walk out of the door, and unlicensed software invites an expensive audit from the vendor.

risk: Major technology programmes overrun, deliver less than promised, or go live without controls, and the business case is never revisited.
audit_objective: Assess whether technology investment is governed, controlled and delivering the promised benefit.
what_to_review: Business case approval, benefit definition and post-implementation review
Governance structure, reporting accuracy and escalation
Scope, schedule and cost control including change requests
Controls designed into new systems before go-live
Data migration accuracy and reconciliation
procedures: Compare reported project status to underlying evidence — status reporting is frequently optimistic until it is not.
Test change requests for approval and their cumulative effect on cost and scope against the original approval.
Test whether internal audit or a controls function reviewed the design before go-live.
For completed migrations, test the reconciliation between source and target data.
Compare realised benefits to the business case for completed projects.
red_flags: Status reported green until it turns red without an amber stage
Benefits never measured after go-live
Controls deferred to a later phase that never arrives
Migration reconciliations performed on counts, not values
evidence: Project status reports and steering minutes
plain: Large technology projects fail slowly and quietly, and status reports stay green until the day they do not.

risk: Material financial reporting depends on spreadsheets and databases built outside IT, with no version control, no testing and no backup.
audit_objective: Assess whether critical end user computing applications are identified and controlled proportionately.
what_to_review: Inventory of critical spreadsheets and user-built databases
Access restriction and version control
Formula integrity, input validation and change testing
Reliance placed on them in financial reporting
Backup and key person dependency
procedures: Identify spreadsheets feeding the financial statements or key controls and test whether they appear in any inventory.
Test formula integrity on a sample — check for hard-coded values overwriting formulas and broken ranges.
Test whether access is restricted and whether changes are tracked.
Assess key person dependency — whether anyone else can operate or explain the model.
red_flags: Critical models on a personal drive
Hard-coded plugs inside formula columns
No one but the author understands the calculation
Versions distinguished only by filename suffix
plain: A surprising amount of financial reporting depends on a spreadsheet on one person's drive with no version control.

risk: Technology decisions are made without alignment to business need or risk appetite, leaving critical dependencies and obsolescence unmanaged.
audit_objective: Assess whether technology is governed, funded and resourced against the organisation's actual dependency on it.
what_to_review: IT strategy and its alignment to business plans
Technology risk reporting to the board and its quality
Technical debt and obsolescence in critical systems
Resourcing, key person dependency and succession
Business continuity for technology-dependent processes
procedures: Compare the technology risk reported to the board against what the audit found operationally.
Identify critical systems past supported life and test the remediation plan and its funding.
Assess key person dependencies for critical platforms and whether documentation would allow another person to operate them.
Test whether business continuity plans for technology-dependent processes have been exercised.
red_flags: Board reporting consistently green while incidents continue
Remediation plans without budget attached
One person holding all knowledge of a critical platform
Continuity plans that assume systems will be available
plain: Old systems that nobody wants to touch keep running until the day they cannot be fixed any more.
